attributes.calendar: Road Reckoning (RR), counted from the sealing of the Roadwarden Statute in RR 1
attributes.consequence: the rim-cities were built as ports and are now inland. The crossing is the only thing that still joins them to each other.
attributes.living_memory: none. The last person who had seen standing water on the Meniscus died about eighty years ago.
attributes.mechanism: withdrawal, not catastrophe — a foot of shoreline a year for most of it, then one hot decade at the end that did the rest
attributes.period: RR -160 to RR -10 — roughly a hundred and fifty years, ending about a decade before the Statute was sealed
attributes.residue: crust to the depth of a man's arm over most of the bounds, with brine beneath it in places and, it now appears, fresh water beneath that at the centre
attributes.scale: an inland sea to a salt plain roughly eight hundred miles across

name: The Drying of the Meniscus
summary: The inland sea did not vanish; it withdrew, over about a hundred and fifty years, at a rate a person could live beside without ever quite noticing. Ports became terraces and terraces became rim, and the last standing water went off in a single hot decade, leaving eight hundred miles of crust and a ring of harbour cities with nothing to harbour. Everyone alive learned the plain from a parent who learned it from someone who remembered a shore.
